relevance_note: The paper describes an identifiable patient with HA20 and a printed germline TNFAIP3 variant ("A novel heterozygous variant was identified in TNFAIP3; ENST00000237289 c.1906C>T (GRCh37 6:138200488 rs200138929)."), plus two affected children and a father.
method_note: Narrative case report; the paper has no patient tables (Table S1 is a supplementary population-genetics MRF table, not patient data), so every row comes from running text. The Markdown uses U+2009 thin spaces between numbers and units (e.g. "4\u2009years", "40\u2009mg", "8\u2009mg/kg"); spans reproduce them exactly. Labels: the proband is called only 'the patient'/'the proband'/'the index case', so rule 5 gives 'patient'; the children are labelled from the printed words 'a boy'/'a girl' plus the related person ('boy of patient', 'girl of patient'); the father is 'father of patient'. Variant rows for the two children keep variant_original_string 'not reported' because the paper ties TNFAIP3 to family members only through "Genetic analysis of family members found segregation with the inflammatory clinical phenotypes (Figure 1A)." (variant description only in a figure); this rests on segregation, not on a printed genotype, and is the least certain part of the extraction. The father is not recorded as carrying the variant (no testing stated; "the details of symptoms and investigations leading to his diagnosis are lacking"). Previously published people: the 7-month-old Japanese child (16) and the patient with TNFAIP3 deletion (8) each get a row (age/ethnicity/feature/variant given); the case in reference 15 and the 22 cases in reference 6 give no individual-level facts and get no rows. age_at_diagnosis for the proband is the clinical AOSD diagnosis age (21); no age at genetic diagnosis is stated. "no obvious intraabdominal pathology" is recorded as an excluded feature written as the paper writes it (a normal investigation as a whole) and is not used to exclude any checklist item. Checklist 'recurrent fever' for the proband is marked observed on the basis of fever at presentation and "multiple hospital admission with similar presentation"; the paper never uses the word 'recurrent' for her. Checklist 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' for the ref [16.] patient is marked observed from "features suggestive of autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome", which is a suggestive rather than confirmed statement. No contradictions inside the paper were found.
